An object falls from rest towards the ground.
Air resistance is negligible.
Which graph shows the variation of the momentum p of the object with time t until it hits the
ground?

hints: Notice the object falls from rest, so check what the value of $p$ must be at $t=0$ on each $p$ against $t$ graph.
Connect momentum $p=mv$ to velocity for free fall with negligible air resistance, where acceleration is the constant $g$ and $v=gt$.
Use $F=dp/dt$ for the $p$-$t$ graph: constant weight $mg$ means constant gradient, so decide which shape has a constant non-zero gradient from the origin.
walkthrough: Identify the motion: from rest with negligible air resistance, the only force is weight $mg$ downward, so acceleration is constant $g$.
State the momentum rule: $p=mv$, where $m$ is constant and $v$ is the instantaneous downward speed.
Use constant acceleration from rest: $v=u+at$ with $u=0$ and $a=g$ gives $v=gt$.
Substitute into momentum: $p=m(gt)=(mg)t$. Since $m$ and $g$ are constants, $p$ is directly proportional to $t$.
Check the graph features: $p=0$ at $t=0$ and $p$ increases with constant gradient equal to the constant force $mg$, which is a straight line through the origin. This is option C.

A.explanation: A horizontal line means constant non-zero $p$ from $t=0$. The object falls from rest so $p=0$ at $t=0$ and then increases as it speeds up.

B.explanation: This curve starts at zero but its gradient decreases, which would mean the rate of gain of momentum decreases. With negligible air resistance the resultant force $mg$ is constant.

C.explanation: With constant acceleration $g$, velocity $v=gt$ so $p=mv=mgt$, a straight line through the origin with constant gradient $mg$.

D.explanation: This curve has increasing gradient, which would mean increasing acceleration. Free fall has constant acceleration $g$, not increasing acceleration.
